notes: Version 2.0 is a status correction. It withdraws the Level 1 theorem of version 1 (no dimensional parameter independent of the Born–Infeld constant c_BI can enter the admissibility constraints), its corollary on fields with independent dimensional couplings, and the application to Reissner–Nordström and Schwarzschild–de Sitter exteriors. The proof rested on premises that the cited papers do not contain: a power law for the pair capacity determined by the admissibility structure (O24 states none; it reports a finite-window fitted exponent requiring confirmation), a continuum limit (Q5a proves convergence of the admissibility form to the zero form and leaves the spatial limit open), a requirement of equal admissibility weights on a fibre (ENI states none), and Foundation axioms A3 and A4 fixing a unique primitive scale (A3 is non-premature selection and A4 projection locking; both refer to the capacity saturation threshold, neither states the amplitude bound or a single-scale condition). Its three cases also have internal gaps: a depth-dependent factor need not change a power-law exponent, a configuration weight does not make the projection injective, and the case split was not exhaustive; the Reissner–Nordström / Schwarzschild–de Sitter application was internally inconsistent. The failure of the proof does not show that every Level 1 property is false; the question is recorded as open, with no conditional theorem in its place. The version keeps dimensional observations: the model fixes relations between dimensions ([c_BI] = [φ][τ]^-1 from the capacity axiom; [A_n] = [φ] and [λ_n] = [τ]^-2 under O20's derivation of the amplitude bound) but not the physical dimension of c_BI, and the white paper's reading of c_BI as a speed is not imported by the current axiom, a gap and inconsistency recorded rather than filled; the definition of an independent dimensional parameter is stated relative to a supplied dimensional assignment; the definition is adequate only when the dimensions of the spectral data are multiples of that of c_BI, in particular when they are dimensionless; under such an assignment, and if the bound's right-hand side is a quantity of the amplitude's dimension, a constant factor depending only on a parameter whose dimension lies outside the span of the bound's ingredients cannot make the bound depend on that parameter, and a dimensionless factor rescales c_BI (corrected from a square root in version 1). The Level 1 / Level 2 distinction is kept, Level 2 being intended as the stronger property; both levels are open. The statement that the Gram rigidity classification is derived under the Born–Infeld bound is withdrawn: that classification is character-theoretic and scale-free. The attribution to Q6b of a Schwarzschild uniqueness result is removed. The version adds a labelled interpretation, a conclusion, primary references on dimensional analysis (Buckingham; Bridgman), refreshed bibliography titles, and a font and Unicode-extraction preamble.
